detail.title: Autonomous Identification of Research Problems
detail.question: How can an autonomous system distinguish a significant, novel research problem from routine tasks?
detail.reason: Autonomous problem selection requires rigorous differentiation between system failures (drift) and genuine scientific gaps.

detail.summary: This revised notebook addresses the technical criteria for distinguishing discovery problems. It identifies that novelty can be mapped by projecting existing research into a multi-dimensional space (such as the 9 dimensions for Comm-MADRL). Problems that fall into uncharted areas of this space, or where agents must switch from collaborative to competitive modes, represent potential areas for significant, novel inquiry.
detail.reason: Provides a structural basis (the 9 dimensions) for identifying where 'new' problems exist relative to established work.

detail.summary: AI in science is conceptually categorized into roles: tools, enablers, and the emerging, hypothetical role of an autonomous agent of understanding. While AI shows promise in optimizing processes, true autonomous scientific discovery remains an aspirational capability requiring further characterization.
